strings.pf.tip.antivirus.body: Your antivirus scans each of Rust’s thousands of files as they load. Add an exclusion for the panel’s server folder (Avast/AVG: Settings → General → Exceptions; Windows Defender: Windows Security → Virus protection → Exclusions). It often halves startup time.
strings.pf.tip.disk.title: Loading files took {s} s
strings.pf.tip.disk.body: Rust reads about 10 GB at startup. On a spinning hard drive that’s slow; an SSD or NVMe is several times faster. If you can, install the panel on an SSD.

strings.pf.tip.mapgen.body: Normal the first time after a wipe or seed change: later startups load the generated map and are much faster. Don’t delete the .map files unless you’re wiping.

strings.pf.tip.pluginerr.body: Oxide or Carbon retry compiling them, which lengthens startup. Find them in the Console, update them in Plugins or disable them.
strings.pf.tip.plugins.title: Many plugins ({n})
strings.pf.tip.plugins.body: Each plugin compiles at startup. Remove the ones you don’t use in Plugins. Carbon usually loads plugins faster than Oxide.
strings.pf.tip.ram.title: Little free RAM at startup ({gb} GB)
strings.pf.tip.ram.body: Rust needs about 8–12 GB. With less, the system uses the disk as memory and everything slows down. Close browsers, games and other programs while it starts, or add RAM.

strings.pf.tip.priority.body: If the server shares the machine with other programs, high priority (below) makes the system favour it.

strings.dc.guide: How to create the bot (5 minutes)
strings.dc.steps:
• Go to discord.com/developers/applications and click New Application.
  • Under Bot, click Reset Token and copy the token. Paste it here.
  • On that same page enable Message Content Intent (needed to send Discord messages into the game).
  • In Discord, enable Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode, right-click the channel and choose Copy Channel ID. Paste it here.
  • Save, and once it says “Connected”, click Invite the bot to your Discord.
strings.dc.cmdsList:
• /estado, /jugadores, /wipe: everyone.
  • /say, /kick, /ban, /vip, /tickets: only members who can kick members in your Discord (change it in Server Settings → Integrations).
  • Every action is recorded in the panel’s activity log.

wiki.title: Getting started
wiki.html:
Scrapwarden installs your Rust server, starts it and lets you manage it from the browser on any device.

  1. In Installation, choose Windows or Linux and click Install server. The progress bar shows the percentage, the amount downloaded and the time left.
  2. If you want plugins, install Oxide or Carbon (only one).
  3. Check the name, map and players in Server settings.
  4. Click Start at the top right. The first time, the map takes a few minutes to generate; when the indicator turns to Running, you're ready.

For your friends to join, open the ports listed in Installation and share the client.connect command from the header (one click copies it).

wiki.title: Installation and updates
wiki.html:
Operating system. By default the panel machine's system is used. You can choose the other one to prepare a server and copy it to another machine, but it can only be started on the same system.

Progress bar. Shows the current phase (SteamCMD download, disk allocation, download, verification and install), the overall percentage, the data downloaded and an estimate of the time left. It also appears in the header and the side menu so you can follow it from any section.

Updating. Rust releases a forced update on the first Thursday of every month. Stop the server and click Update server; Oxide or Carbon are reinstalled automatically. You can also turn on automatic updates in the Scheduler.

Verify files compares everything with Steam and repairs damaged files; it takes a bit longer.

Framework. Oxide is the standard; Carbon is faster and loads almost all uMod plugins. Back to vanilla removes them without deleting your plugins.

Already have a server?

At the top of Install, choose how you want to use the panel:

  • I already have one here: type the folder that contains RustDedicated (or use Browse) and click Detect. The panel reads your .bat or .sh start script (ports, identity, RCON password, name, map and seed) and server.cfg, and keeps the other parameters as extra arguments. Nothing is reinstalled or deleted. If the server is already running, the panel connects to it; from then on, start it from the panel.
  • Rented server (RCON): enter the IP, RCON port and password from your host and click Test. Console, players, chat, moderation, F7 tickets, /staff, watch, statistics, Discord, Tebex, VIP, rates and the public page all work. Installing, plugins, backups and wipes are handled by your host. For the map and everything else that uses the plugin, download ScrapwardenBridge.cs and upload it over FTP to the plugins folder. Restarts save and shut the server down so your host starts it again.

wiki.title: Existing or rented server
wiki.html:
Install offers three ways to start:

  • Install a new one: the panel downloads Rust on this machine.
  • I already have one here: pick the server folder. The panel reads the .bat/.sh and server.cfg, detects Oxide or Carbon and keeps the map, plugins and any parameters it does not manage. If the server is already running, it connects without restarting it.
  • Rented server (RCON): enter the IP, RCON port and password from your host. Console, players, moderation, F7, statistics, Discord, Tebex, VIP and rates work. Starting, installing, backups and wipes stay with your host. "Restart" saves and shuts the server down so the host starts it again.

FTP/SFTP access (optional): in remote mode, add your host's FTP or SFTP details (protocol, user, password and the folder that contains RustDedicated). Press Test: it should find the executable or the server folder. You can then install, enable, disable and configure plugins from Plugins, and the panel uploads and updates ScrapwardenBridge.cs itself. Disabled plugins are kept in oxide/plugins_disabled (or carbon/…).

Use SFTP if your host offers it: FTP without TLS sends the password unencrypted.

wiki.title: Overview
wiki.html:
The header always shows the server status, its name, the connect command, the map and the Start, Restart and Stop buttons.

  • Indicators: players and queue, server FPS and entities, CPU and memory, with a trend chart of up to 5 minutes. FPS below 20 is highlighted in amber.
  • Message to all: writes in the in-game chat.
  • Save the world writes the map to disk immediately.
  • Restart with warning: warns in chat every minute and restarts when the countdown ends.
  • Force close: only if the server stops responding; anything since the last save is lost.

wiki.title: Statistics
wiki.html:
Statistics shows how your server evolves. While the server is running, the panel stores a sample every 5 minutes and playtime every minute. Data is kept for 90 days in data/stats.json.

  • Period: 24 h, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or this wipe (since the last manual or automatic wipe).
  • Indicators: online now, peak, average, unique players (and how many had played before), newcomers, hours played, average and minimum FPS, and kills.
  • Players online: chart of the average per interval; hover to see the peak and queue. Gaps are periods when the server was off.
  • When your players are online: heatmap by weekday and hour over at least the last 4 weeks. Use it to pick wipe or event times.
  • Daily activity: unique and new players per day.
  • FPS and entities: to spot performance drops through the wipe.
  • Rankings: most time played and most kills (kills need Oxide or Carbon with the plugin). Click a name to open their profile.

wiki.title: Performance and startup
wiki.html:
The Performance section measures how long the server takes to start and watches it once running.

Last startup: total time until ready and a bar with each phase detected in the server log: starting the process, loading game files, map and world, uploading the map to Facepunch, and Oxide/Carbon with plugins. While it starts, the bar moves live.

How to speed it up: tips based on what was seen in that startup. The most important:

  • Antivirus: add an exclusion for the panel’s server folder. On Windows this usually saves the most time.
  • Map upload failed ([Rust.MapCache] Failed to upload map file): allow RustDedicated.exe out to the Internet in the firewall and antivirus.
  • Disk: an SSD loads Rust several times faster than a spinning drive.
  • RAM: Rust needs about 8–12 GB free.
  • Generated map: only slow the first time after a wipe; afterwards it loads from disk.
  • Plugins: remove unused ones and fix those that fail to compile.

High priority: makes the system favour the Rust server. On Linux it needs administrator rights; otherwise the panel applies “above normal”.

Performance alerts: notify the panel and Discord if FPS stay below a threshold for several minutes, if server RAM exceeds a share of the machine, or if the server freezes (process alive but not responding). You can have it restart automatically when it freezes or when FPS stay low.

wiki.title: Live map
wiki.html:
Shows your server's map with player positions, refreshed every 3 seconds. Each team has its own colour.

  • Moving around: drag to pan and use the wheel (or + and -) to zoom. The fit button returns to the full view.
  • Layers: names, sleepers, events (cargo ship, helicopter, Bradley and Chinook), monuments and the Rust grid. Hovering shows the grid square and coordinates.
  • Players: click one to see their status, grid and teammates, and open their inventory or history, kick or ban them. In Players and Watch, the locate button takes you straight to them.
  • Search: type a name to centre the map on that player.

The server draws the image the first time and it's saved; it's regenerated automatically after a wipe or a seed change. Requires Oxide or Carbon with the ScrapwardenBridge add-on.

In-game style layers: roads, railways, rivers and power lines are drawn over the map using the server’s real routes, and monuments have icons. Toggle each layer at the top; the legend explains them. They need the ScrapwardenBridge plugin 1.5 or later (the panel updates it automatically); if the map was drawn earlier, click “Redraw”.

wiki.title: Console
wiki.html:
Shows the server log, chat and panel messages in real time. You can filter by source or text and turn off Follow output to read calmly.

Type RCON commands in the bottom bar; the up and down arrows bring back previous ones. There's a list of useful commands at the end of this wiki.

wiki.title: Chat
wiki.html:
Everything written on the server is saved (up to 20,000 messages) and arrives in real time.

  • Filters: all, global, team, flagged (with forbidden words) and private messages sent from the panel. The search finds text or names across the whole history.
  • Click a name to send them a private message, see only their messages, mute or warn them, open their profile, see them on the map or kick them.
  • Writing: at the bottom choose whether the message goes to everyone or privately to an online player (private messages require the ScrapwardenBridge add-on).

Flagged messages appear in amber and blocked ones in red and struck through: nobody else saw them.

wiki.title: Players
wiki.html:
List of online players with ping, time and health. From each row you can open their inventory, kick or ban them (you're asked for a reason, which the player will see).

Manage by SteamID also works for offline players: ban, unban, give or remove admin and moderator, and give items by short name (for example rifle.ak or wood).

The banned list lets you unban with one click. Admin and ban changes are saved to the server configuration automatically.

wiki.title: Teams and team limit
wiki.html:
In Players you'll see every team with its members, who is online and quick access to their inventory. It refreshes every 2 minutes.

If your server has a limit (for example “Max 3”), set it in Watch → Team limit:

  • Team over the limit: a serious alert as soon as a team goes over the maximum.
  • Groups sharing cupboards: players from different teams (or no team) authorised on the same cupboards, the most common way to get around the limit. Review it calmly: after a raid, attackers sometimes authorise on the victim's cupboard.

wiki.title: Moderation: mutes, warnings, notes and temporary bans
wiki.html:
Each player has a profile (Profile button in Players, the chat or Watch) with their history, Steam data and moderation:

  • Mute for 5 minutes to 1 day, or indefinitely. The player gets a notice and it's lifted automatically when time is up.
  • Warn with a reason the player sees in chat. Warnings expire after the days you choose.
  • Automatic sanctions: for example, 2 warnings mute for 1 hour, 3 give a 1-day temporary ban and 5 a permanent ban. Set them in Chat → Sanctions for warnings.
  • Internal notes: only the team sees them, with author and date (for example “suspected ESP, check tomorrow”).
  • Temporary ban from 1 hour to 30 days. They're unbanned automatically when it ends, even if the panel restarted.

Word filter: in Chat, type the forbidden words (with * as a wildcard, ignoring case and accents). With the add-on, the message is blocked before anyone sees it; you can also warn, mute or kick automatically.

The badges next to each name show active warnings, mute and number of notes.

wiki.title: Inventory viewer
wiki.html:
Open the inventory of any player, online or sleeping on the map, with the Inventory button in Players, Watch or the history.

  • Each item is shown with its image (loaded from an external website; change it in Settings › Item images) or, if it fails to load, with its name.
  • You see the inventory (24 slots), clothing and belt, with the amount and a condition bar under each item (green, amber or red).
  • Click an item to see its internal name, condition, ammo, attachments and skin.
  • Remove item deletes it; Clear inventory deletes everything (you have to click twice).

Requires Oxide or Carbon with the ScrapwardenBridge add-on, which the panel installs by itself. The inventory is a snapshot: click Refresh to see changes.

wiki.title: Watch and anti-cheat
wiki.html:
Analyses what happens on the server and raises low, medium or high severity alerts. New ones appear instantly, with a counter in the menu; serious ones also pop up.

DetectionWhat it looks at
AimHeadshot percentage over the last 50 hits on players.
DistanceHits further than normal for the weapon (stricter for pistols, SMGs, shotguns and bows).
AntihackRust antihack violations (FlyHack, SpeedHack, NoClip…) within 10 minutes.
KillsPlayers killed within 10 minutes.
F7 reportsEvery report; serious if several players report them within an hour.
Shared IP and ban evasionAccounts from the same IP, especially a banned player's. Works without plugins.

On each alert you can see the inventory, the player's history (names, IPs, stats and alerts), kick, ban or mark it as reviewed. Players to watch ranks them by suspicion level.

Tune the thresholds to your server and, if you like, paste a Discord webhook to get alerts in a channel. Remember: an alert is not proof; lag causes false violations and good players hit a lot. Watch them (for example with spectate) before banning.

wiki.title: Steam profile checks
wiki.html:
When a player connects, the panel looks up their Steam profile and applies your rules. Many cheaters come back with new accounts after a ban; this helps stop them.

  1. Get a free key at steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey (it asks for a domain: any will do).
  2. Paste it in Watch → Steam profile checks and turn the checks on.
  3. For each rule choose Do nothing, Alert (creates an alert) or Kick (kicks them with a message in the notification language and creates the alert).
RuleWhat it checks
Recent bansVAC or game bans within the days you choose.
CommunityAccounts restricted by Steam.
New accountCreated fewer days ago than you choose.
Few hoursFewer hours in Rust than set (only if the player shows them).
Private profileHides account age and hours.

Add your friends or staff to the whitelist so they're never checked. Results are kept for 24 hours and appear in each player's history, where you can check again.

wiki.title: VPN, hosting and country detection
wiki.html:
In Watch, the VPN, proxy and country section checks each player's IP when they connect (results are cached for 3 days).

  • Provider: proxycheck.io (1,000 free queries a day with a key; better VPN detection) or ip-api.com (no key, non-commercial use only).
  • VPN / proxy, hosting IP and country: for each, choose do nothing, alert or kick. Alerts appear in Watch and on Discord.
  • Countries: a list of codes (US, DE, BR…) in block mode or allow-only mode.
  • Whitelist: SteamIDs or IPs that are never checked (staff, friends on a VPN).

Private or local IPs are not checked. For players with recent game bans, use Steam profile checks.

wiki.title: F7 reports (tickets)
wiki.html:
Every time a player presses F7 and reports someone, a ticket opens. Later reports about the same player are added to the open ticket, so you can see at a glance how many different players complain. The same report repeated within a minute is not counted twice. Requires ScrapwardenBridge.

  • Take it: assigns the ticket to you (it becomes “In progress”) so the rest of the staff knows someone is on it.
  • Staff notes: write down what you check; they stay on the ticket.
  • Player file: history, alerts and previous sanctions.
  • Close ticket: pick the outcome (no action, warning, mute, kick, temporary ban or ban). The sanction is applied right away and stored in the player file like any other.

If you tick the box, the reporters get a private message (if online) saying their report was reviewed or acted on, which encourages them to keep reporting. The menu counter shows unassigned tickets. In Discord, /tickets lists the pending ones.

wiki.title: Shared bans
wiki.html:
Scrapwarden works as a Centralized Banning server, Rust's official feature: when a player joins, the server asks the panel whether they are banned. It works on vanilla, no plugins.

  1. In Shared bans → Settings, enable the list. If this panel manages the server, it is set up automatically (server.bansServerEndpoint).
  2. For other servers (yours or friends'), set the panel public address, click Add server and paste the command into its console and its server.cfg. Each server has its own secret key, which you can change or remove.

The list includes your server's bans (with reason and expiry), the ones you add in the panel for every server and, optionally, mutes. Removing a server ban also unbans the player.

External lists: add the address of another list in the same format (another Scrapwarden, your Server Armour organization…). Alert mode creates an alert in Watch; Block stops them joining. Only the SteamID is sent and answers are cached for 15 minutes.

If the panel goes down: with "Let players in", servers keep working with their own bans. Rust only checks on join; if you ban someone who is already in, the panel kicks them from your server.

wiki.title: Plugins
wiki.html:
Require Oxide or Carbon.

  • Installed: version, author and status. You can reload, disable (set aside without deleting), delete with or without their data and configure their JSON with validation; saving creates a .bak copy and reloads.
  • Check for updates compares your versions with uMod and adds an Update button where needed.
  • uMod catalogue: search by name or topic and click Install. It loads instantly if the server is running.
  • Upload file: drag one or more .cs files.

Plugins are code that runs on your server: only install the ones you know.

wiki.title: Permissions
wiki.html:
Plugins use permissions such as kits.vip or teleport.use. You can grant them to a user (SteamID) or to a group. The default group includes every player.

Create groups (for example vip), add players and grant permissions to the group: it's easier to maintain. Look up shows all permissions, those of a user or group, or who has a specific permission.

wiki.title: VIP with expiry
wiki.html:
Put a player into an Oxide/Carbon group (for example vip) for a number of days and the panel removes them automatically when it ends. Ideal for store VIPs or event prizes.

  1. In VIP settings list your groups (the first is the default). Missing groups are created automatically.
  2. In Permissions give each group what your VIP includes (kits, skins, queue priority…).
  3. In Grant VIP choose the player, group and days (0 = permanent). If they were already VIP, the days are added to the time left.

The player gets a message when granted, a warning before it expires (24 h by default) and another when it ends. If the server is off when it expires, it is removed once RCON reconnects. You can also extend or remove it by hand, and from Discord with /vip player days [group]. Every change is stored in the activity log.

Queue priority: with “VIPs skip the queue” enabled, VIP groups get scrapwarden.skipqueue and join even when the server is full. It is the perk that fits a vanilla-style server, because it does not touch gameplay.

wiki.title: Tebex store
wiki.html:
Connect a Tebex store and purchases are delivered automatically, without installing the Tebex plugin or opening ports: the panel checks the Tebex queue every 1-2 minutes, runs each package's commands over RCON and marks them as delivered.

  1. On creator.tebex.io create a Rust store.
  2. In Game Servers → Connect Game Server → Plugin copy the secret key and paste it in Store. It is checked when saving.
  3. Add the commands to each package. {id} is the buyer's SteamID and {username} their name.
To give…Command
Self-expiring VIPscrapwarden.vip {id} vip 30 (group and days; 0 = permanent)
Permanent groupoxide.usergroup add {id} vip
A permissionoxide.grant user {id} kits.vip
An iteminventory.giveto {id} rifle.ak 1 (tick “when the player is online”)

“Online” commands wait until the buyer connects; “immediately” ones run right away. If the server is off, everything waits in Tebex and is delivered when it is back. Each delivery shows in the Deliveries table, in the activity log (user tebex) and, optionally, with a thank-you in chat and a Discord notice. Use oxide. or c. depending on your framework. Do not run the official Tebex plugin with the same key at the same time, or purchases would be delivered twice.

wiki.title: In-game staff (/staff)
wiki.html:
Gives your moderators and admins a window inside the game so they can work without leaving Rust. Requires ScrapwardenBridge 1.6 or later.

  1. In In-game staff, add the player (online player name or SteamID64) and choose a level. The panel grants scrapwarden.mod or scrapwarden.admin on the server.
  2. In game, type /staff. A window opens with the Players, Reports and, for admins, World tabs.
LevelCan
ModeratorSee and close F7 reports (no action, warning or kick), go to a player, warn, mute for 30 min, unmute and kick. Gets a chat notice for each F7.
AdminEverything above, plus 1-day, 7-day or permanent bans, bring a player, heal, day/night, clear/storm and events (cargo, heli, airdrop, Chinook).

Kicks and bans need a second click. Sanctions are carried out by the panel, so they show up in the player file and in the activity log as ingame:Name. If someone has the permission set by hand but is not on the panel list, their actions are ignored. Removing someone from the list revokes the permissions.

wiki.title: Server settings
wiki.html:
• Identity: name, description, website, header image (1024×512), max players and data folder.
  • Map: procedural or special maps. Size (1000 to 6000) and seed define the map; changing them creates a new one.
  • Network: game, query, Rust+ and RCON ports, RCON password and Steam branch.
  • Startup: extra parameters (for example +decay.scale 0.5), start with the panel and automatic restart if the server crashes.

Changes apply on the next restart.

wiki.title: Rates, PvP/PvE mode and world
wiki.html:
Rates & world lets you control how your server plays without touching files.

Game mode: click PvP or PvE. It applies instantly over RCON (server.pve), without a restart, and is kept for future starts. The chip next to the server name shows the current mode and rates.

Multipliers (need Oxide or Carbon with the ScrapwardenBridge plugin):

  • Gathering: trees, rocks, ore nodes and animals.
  • Pickups: hemp, mushrooms, loose stones and wood, and crops.
  • Quarries: quarries, excavator and survey charges.
  • Crafting speed: 2x takes half the time.

Use the presets (Vanilla, 2x, 3x, 5x, 10x) or adjust each slider. The plugin stores the values and the panel sends them again every time the server starts.

Vanilla settings (no plugin): decay (decay.scale), tool cupboard upkeep, radiation, stability and locked crate hack time.

World (server must be running):

  • Time: dawn, noon, dusk or night in one click, and freeze time.
  • Weather: clear, rain, storm, fog or back to automatic weather.
  • Events (with the plugin): cargo ship, patrol helicopter, airdrop and Chinook.

If enabled, the panel announces mode and rate changes in game chat. Add “2x”, “3x”… to the server name in Server settings so it shows in the server browser.

wiki.title: Scheduler
wiki.html:
Add daily restart times. Before each one, players are warned in chat (60, 30, 15, 10, 5, 3, 2 and 1 minutes, up to the chosen lead time). Each restart can make a backup and update Rust and the framework.

Automatic announcements repeat every set number of minutes; they support colours such as <color=#5bb5a2>text</color>.

wiki.title: Backups and wipe
wiki.html:
A backup stores the map, player data and plugins with their configuration. You can download, restore (with the server stopped) or delete it. The oldest ones are removed automatically according to the number to keep.

Wipe (server stopped): a map wipe deletes the world and buildings; a full wipe also deletes blueprints. You can generate a new seed and make an automatic backup first.

wiki.title: Wipe scheduler
wiki.html:
The wipe scheduler runs wipes for you and warns your players.

  • Forced wipe: Facepunch forces a wipe on the first Thursday of every month at 19:00 London time. The panel works it out automatically, including daylight saving.
  • Frequency: monthly (forced only), weekly or every two weeks on the day and time you choose. Your own wipe is skipped in the forced-wipe week.
  • Blueprints: wipe them only on the forced wipe, on every wipe, or never.
  • What it does: announces in chat 24 h, 1 h and in the final minutes; saves the world, stops the server, makes a backup, updates the server and Oxide/Carbon on the forced wipe, deletes the map (and blueprints when due), sets a new seed and starts again. When done it notifies Discord.
  • Delay after the forced wipe: waits a few minutes after the official time so the Oxide or Carbon update is out.
  • Skip: skip a specific wipe from the upcoming list.

The countdown also appears next to the server name. If the panel was off at wipe time, it runs the wipe on return if less than 2 hours have passed; otherwise it is logged as missed.

wiki.title: Public page
wiki.html:
The public page is a page for your players, no login needed, at http://your-ip:8080/server. Turn it on in Public page and share the link on Discord or in your server description.

  • What it shows: status and players online, a Connect with Steam button and the client.connect command, next wipe countdown, PvP/PvE, rates, team limit, weekly activity with the busiest time, current map with monuments and routes, rankings, rules and your links (Discord, store, website, Steam group).
  • Privacy: it never shows player positions, IPs, SteamIDs or moderation data. Online player names appear only if you enable it.
  • Connect address: set your public IP or domain. If empty, the address used to open the page is used.
  • Language: the visitor’s or a fixed one; visitors can switch it at the top.

To reach it from outside your network, the panel port (8080) must be open, ideally behind an HTTPS proxy. The page refreshes itself every 30 seconds.

wiki.title: Discord bot
wiki.html:
The Discord bot connects your server and your Discord both ways.

  • Chat: in-game global chat appears in the channel you choose, and what’s written there reaches the game as [Discord] name: message. Team chat is never posted, and the word filter also applies to Discord messages.
  • Commands: /estado, /jugadores and /wipe for everyone; /say, /kick and /ban only for members who can kick in your Discord. Every action is logged in the activity log as discord:user.
  • Bot status: shows how many players are online.

Setup: create an application at discord.com/developers, copy the bot token, enable Message Content Intent, copy the channel ID (with Discord developer mode) and paste everything in Discord bot. When it says “Connected”, use the button to invite it to your server. The token is stored only on your machine and never shown again.

wiki.title: Account and language
wiki.html:
Panel language: change it from the selector in the side menu, the sign-in screen or this section. Each browser remembers it.

Notification language: what players see in chat (restart warnings and kick messages) and the language of Discord alerts.

Sound: a cinematic impact plays in sync with the intro animation when the panel opens: a riser while the logo draws and a deep metallic hit when “PANEL” appears. Browsers block audio until you interact with the page, so if it doesn't play on load it will play when you sign in. Turn it on or off here (saved per browser) and use “Test” to hear it.

Password: at least 8 characters. After 5 failed attempts, access is locked for 5 minutes. If an administrator forgets theirs, an owner can change it in Administrators. If the only owner forgets it, stop the panel, delete the "users" list from data/config.json and you'll be able to create a new owner when you sign in again.

If you upgraded from an earlier version with a single password, your username is admin with the same password.

Support the project: Scrapwarden is free and open source. If it helps you, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi (also via the ☕ link at the bottom of the menu).

wiki.title: Administrators and activity log
wiki.html:
Everyone who manages the server can have their own username and password, with one of these roles:

RoleWhat they can do
OwnerEverything, including managing administrators.
AdministratorEverything except managing administrators.
ModeratorView the panel, kick, mute, warn, ban, write in chat, view inventories and review alerts.
ViewerView only.

Buttons a role can't use don't appear. Changing someone's role or password closes their sessions. There must always be at least one owner.

The activity log records who made each change, when, on what and whether it worked, including attempts without permission. Passwords and keys are never stored in the log.

wiki.title: Two-step verification
wiki.html:
Protects your account even if someone finds out your password: signing in also asks for a 6-digit code from your phone.

  1. Install an authenticator app: Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy or similar.
  2. In Account and language → Two-step verification, click Turn on and scan the QR code.
  3. Enter the code shown in the app to confirm.
  4. Save the 8 recovery codes: each works once to sign in if you lose your phone. You can generate new ones whenever you like.

If an administrator loses their phone and codes, an owner can remove their two-step verification in Administrators. It's highly recommended if the panel is reachable from the internet.

wiki.title: Troubleshooting
wiki.html:
Found a bug? Click Report a bug at the bottom of the side menu: GitHub opens with the version and technical details already filled in, without IPs or player data.

  • Nobody can join: check the firewall and router ports (game and query over UDP) and that you share the public IP.
  • RCON doesn't connect: wait for the map to finish generating; if it still doesn't connect, check that no other program uses the RCON port.
  • Installation stuck at 0 %: SteamCMD is updating itself; wait a couple of minutes. If it fails, click Install again with Verify files on.
  • A plugin doesn't load: look for the compile error in the console; it's usually an outdated plugin version.
  • Inventories or watch don't work: in Watch, check that the ScrapwardenBridge add-on is installed and responding.
  • Low FPS: reduce the map size or max players, review heavy plugins and the entity count.
